question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with the Separation of judiciary from executive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 50 of the Indian Constitution states: "The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State." (अनुच्छेद 50 — न्यायपालिका को कार्यपालिका से पृथक करना)

 

• Article 50 falls under Part IV of the Constitution, which deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs).

 

• The objective of this article is to ensure the independence of the judiciary so that judicial functions are not influenced by the executive branch of the government.

 

• Being a DPSP, Article 50 is not enforceable by any court, but it is fundamental in the governance of the country and the State is expected to apply this principle in making laws.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The separation of judiciary from executive has largely been implemented in India through the Code of Criminal Procedure, which separates the judicial and executive magistracy.

 

• Other important DPSPs include Article 39 (equal pay for equal work, distribution of resources), Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code), and Article 48 (organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 41 (Option 1): Deals with the right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases like unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement.

 

• Article 51 (Option 2): Deals with the promotion of international peace and security, and directs the State to foster respect for international law and treaty obligations.

 

• Article 40 (Option 3): Directs the State to organise village panchayats and endow them with powers to function as units of self-government.

question: World Bank approved USD 350 million aid in May 2022 for the “Systems Reform Endeavors for Transformed Health Achievement” (SRESTHA) for ______ state in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The World Bank approved a USD 350 million loan for the "Systems Reform Endeavors for Transformed Health Achievement in Gujarat" (SRESTHA-G) project in 2022. (गुजरात राज्य के लिए विश्व बैंक की स्वास्थ्य सहायता परियोजना)

 

• The project is aimed at strengthening primary healthcare services and improving disease surveillance systems in the state of Gujarat.

 

• It supports Gujarat's health system to become more resilient, better prepared for future health emergencies, and to improve access to quality primary healthcare for citizens, especially in underserved areas.

 

• The project is implemented with support from the Government of Gujarat in partnership with the World Bank.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The World Bank has funded several state-specific health system strengthening projects in India, such as similar reform projects for Karnataka and other states in earlier years.

 

• SRESTHA-G focuses on three key areas: strengthening service delivery, enhancing public health surveillance, and improving governance and management of the health system in Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Punjab was not the recipient of the SRESTHA-G project; the state has separately received World Bank support for other sectors such as agriculture and water resources.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Himachal Pradesh was not the recipient of this particular World Bank health aid project in May 2022.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Bihar was not the recipient of the SRESTHA-G project; Bihar has had separate World Bank-funded projects in areas such as rural livelihoods and disaster resilience.

question: The ______ of a ray is the angle measured from the reflected ray to the normal surface.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Angle of Reflection.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Angle of Reflection is the angle measured between the reflected ray and the normal (an imaginary line perpendicular to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence). (परावर्तन कोण — परावर्तित किरण और अभिलंब के बीच का कोण)

 

• According to the Laws of Reflection, the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection.

 

• Both the incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal lie in the same plane at the point of incidence.

 

• This concept is fundamental to understanding how light behaves when it strikes a smooth surface such as a mirror.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Angle of Incidence is measured between the incident ray (the ray falling on the surface) and the normal — it is the counterpart of the angle of reflection.

 

• Mirrors that produce this predictable reflection (angle of incidence = angle of reflection) are said to undergo regular reflection, as opposed to diffused/irregular reflection from rough surfaces.

 

NOTE

 

• Angle of Diffusion (Option 1): This is not a standard term in geometric optics for light reflection; diffusion generally refers to scattering of light in multiple directions from a rough surface.

 

• Angle of Incidence (Option 3): This is the angle between the incident ray (falling on the surface) and the normal, not the reflected ray.

 

• Angle of Refraction (Option 4): This is the angle between the refracted ray (the ray that bends while passing from one medium to another) and the normal, applicable in refraction, not reflection.

question: ______ won the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Max Verstappen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing) won the 2022 Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix, held at the Suzuka Circuit on 9 October 2022. (मैक्स वेरस्टापेन — 2022 जापानी ग्रांड प्री विजेता)

 

• This victory also confirmed Max Verstappen as the 2022 Formula 1 World Drivers' Champion, his second consecutive title.

 

• The race was affected by heavy rain, and it was one of the shortest races in F1 history in terms of racing laps completed under a time-limited format.

 

• Verstappen drives for the Red Bull Racing team and is from the Netherlands.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Max Verstappen went on to win the F1 World Championship again in 2023 and 2024, becoming a multiple-time World Champion.

 

• Suzuka Circuit in Japan is known for its unique figure-eight layout and is one of the most technically demanding circuits on the F1 calendar.

 

NOTE

 

• Charles Leclerc (Option 1): A Ferrari driver from Monaco; he did not win the 2022 Japanese Grand Prix.

 

• Sergio Perez (Option 2): Verstappen's Red Bull Racing teammate from Mexico; he finished behind Verstappen in this race.

 

• Carlos Sainz Jr. (Option 4): A Ferrari driver from Spain; he did not win the 2022 Japanese Grand Prix.

question: Which city existed in the Indus valley civilization?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harappa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harappa was one of the major cities of the Indus Valley Civilization, situated on the banks of the Ravi river in present-day Punjab province, Pakistan. (हड़प्पा — सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता का प्रमुख नगर)

 

• It was the first site to be discovered (in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni), and the entire civilization is also known as the Harappan Civilization after this site.

 

• The Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2500 BCE) is known for its planned urban settlements, grid-pattern streets, advanced drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures.

 

• Other important Indus Valley sites include Mohenjo-daro (Sindh), Lothal, Dholavira, Kalibangan, and Rakhigarhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mohenjo-daro, meaning "Mound of the Dead," is another key Harappan city, famous for the Great Bath and its advanced urban planning.

 

• Lothal (Gujarat) is notable for having one of the world's earliest known dockyards.

 

NOTE

 

• Dwarka (Option 1): An ancient city in Gujarat associated with Lord Krishna in Hindu mythology; it is not a site of the Indus Valley Civilization.

 

• Sanchi (Option 3): Located in Madhya Pradesh, famous for its Buddhist stupas built during the Mauryan and later periods; it has no connection to the Indus Valley Civilization.

 

• Muziris (Option 4): An ancient port city on the Malabar Coast (Kerala) known for trade with the Roman Empire; it belongs to a much later period, not the Indus Valley Civilization.

question: The JALDOOT application launched in September 2022 is used by Gram Rojgar Sahyak to measure _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is water level in well.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The JALDOOT app was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development in September 2022 to monitor groundwater levels across rural India. (जलदूत ऐप — भूजल स्तर मापने हेतु)

 

• It is used by Gram Rojgar Sahayaks (GRS), functionaries under the MGNREGA scheme, to measure the water level in selected open wells twice a year — once before monsoon and once after monsoon.

 

• The data collected helps in creating a database of groundwater levels across villages, which supports planning for water conservation works under MGNREGA, such as check dams, farm ponds, and percolation tanks.

 

• This initiative supports the broader goal of the Jal Shakti Abhiyan and sustainable groundwater management in rural India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• JALDOOT complements other groundwater monitoring efforts by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), which uses piezometers and observation wells for scientific monitoring.

 

• MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) provides at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment and funds water conservation and afforestation works.

 

NOTE

 

• Rainfall (Option 1): Rainfall is measured using rain gauges by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), not by the JALDOOT app.

 

• crop yield (Option 3): Crop yield estimation is carried out through agricultural surveys and remote sensing by agencies like the Ministry of Agriculture, not through JALDOOT.

 

• Humidity (Option 4): Humidity is measured using hygrometers, typically by meteorological agencies, and is unrelated to the JALDOOT app's purpose.

question: In which year was the Arms Act passed in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1959.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arms Act was passed in 1959 by the Parliament of India. (शस्त्र अधिनियम, 1959)

 

• It regulates matters relating to acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, transport, import, export, and use of arms and ammunition in India.

 

• The Act repealed and replaced the earlier Indian Arms Act of 1878, which had been enacted during the British colonial period.

 

• It works alongside the Arms Rules to provide the licensing framework for firearms in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arms Act, 1959 was later amended, notably by the Arms (Amendment) Act, 2019, which increased penalties for illegal possession of arms and reduced the number of firearms a licensed individual may hold.

 

• The colonial-era Indian Arms Act of 1878 was widely criticised by Indian nationalists, including Mahatma Gandhi, for disarming the native population while allowing the British to remain armed.

 

NOTE

 

• 1951 (Option 1): This year is associated with other laws such as the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, not the Arms Act.

 

• 1955 (Option 2): This year is associated with laws such as the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, not the Arms Act.

 

• 1964 (Option 4): This is not the year the Arms Act was passed; it has no particular association with this legislation.

question: ______ is the key circuit board holding the essential processing parts of a computer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Motherboard.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Motherboard is the main circuit board of a computer that holds and interconnects the essential processing components such as the CPU, RAM, and expansion slots. (मदरबोर्ड — कंप्यूटर का मुख्य परिपथ बोर्ड)

 

• It acts as the backbone of the computer, providing communication pathways (buses) between the processor, memory, and peripheral devices.

 

• All major components — including the Central Processing Unit (CPU), memory (RAM), storage drives, and input/output ports — are either directly mounted on or connected to the motherboard.

 

• It is also called the mainboard, system board, or logic board in different contexts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The motherboard also houses the BIOS/UEFI firmware chip, which initializes hardware during the booting process.

 

• Common motherboard form factors include ATX, Micro-ATX, and Mini-ITX, which determine the size and layout of the board.

 

NOTE

 

• Firmware (Option 1): Firmware is low-level software (like BIOS) permanently programmed into a hardware device to control its basic functions; it is not a circuit board.

 

• Central Processing Unit (Option 2): The CPU is the processor chip itself — the "brain" of the computer — but it is mounted on, not the same as, the motherboard.

 

• Random Access Memory (Option 3): RAM is the temporary, volatile memory used for active data and processes; it is a component installed on the motherboard, not the board itself.

question: Which is the highest plateau in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tibet plateau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tibetan Plateau is the highest plateau in the world, with an average elevation of about 4,500 metres above sea level. (तिब्बत का पठार — विश्व का सबसे ऊँचा पठार)

 

• It is often referred to as the "Roof of the World" because of its extreme altitude and its location surrounded by some of the world's highest mountain ranges, including the Himalayas to the south.

 

• The plateau is the source of several major Asian rivers, including the Indus, Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo), Yangtze, and Yellow River.

 

• It covers a vast area spanning the Tibet Autonomous Region of China and parts of neighbouring regions, making it also the largest plateau in the world by area.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Because of its high average elevation and its role in influencing the Asian monsoon system, the Tibetan Plateau is sometimes also called the "Third Pole," as it holds the largest reserve of ice outside the polar regions.

 

• The Deccan Plateau, by contrast, is a much lower, triangular tableland covering most of peninsular India, with an average elevation of 600–900 metres.

 

NOTE

 

• East African Plateau (Option 1): A significant plateau region in Africa, part of the East African Rift system, but with much lower elevations than the Tibetan Plateau.

 

• Deccan plateau (Option 2): A large plateau covering most of peninsular India, bounded by the Western and Eastern Ghats, with average elevations far lower than the Tibetan Plateau.

 

• Western plateau (Option 3): Not a recognized term for one of the world's major high-altitude plateaus in the same sense as the Tibetan Plateau.

question: Which of the following is not a regional name for East Coast (or part of it) of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malabar Coast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The East Coast of India stretches along the Bay of Bengal, from West Bengal in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, and is known regionally by names such as the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu–Andhra Pradesh stretch), the Tamil Nadu coast, and the Utkal coast (Odisha stretch). (पूर्वी तट के क्षेत्रीय नाम)

 

• The Malabar Coast, by contrast, lies along the West Coast of India, bordering the Arabian Sea, covering the coastline of Kerala and parts of Karnataka.

 

• The East Coast is broader and has a wide continental shelf, in contrast to the narrower West Coast with the Malabar Coast known for lagoons and backwaters like those in Kerala.

 

• Distinguishing East Coast (Bay of Bengal side) from West Coast (Arabian Sea side) regional names is a common static-geography exam theme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Northern Circars is another regional name for part of the East Coast, covering the Andhra Pradesh coastline between the Utkal coast and the Coromandel Coast.

 

• The Konkan Coast is the regional name for the West Coast stretch from Maharashtra to Goa, complementing the Malabar Coast further south.

 

NOTE

 

• Coromandel Coast (Option 1): This is indeed a regional name for the East Coast, referring to the coastline of Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra Pradesh along the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Tamil Nadu coast (Option 2): This is part of the East Coast, forming the southern section of the Coromandel Coast along the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Utkal coast (Option 3): This refers to the coastline of Odisha (historically called Utkal), which is also part of the East Coast along the Bay of Bengal.

question: _________ is an ancient martial art that originated in peninsular India as a part of military training for warriors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalaripayattu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalaripayattu is an ancient martial art that originated in Kerala, in peninsular India, and is considered one of the oldest martial art forms in the world. (कलरीपयट्टु — केरल की प्राचीन युद्धकला)

 

• It was traditionally practiced as part of the military training of warriors and combines strikes, kicks, grappling, weaponry, and healing techniques.

 

• The training is imparted in a specially constructed pit called a "Kalari", which also gives the art form its name.

 

• Kalaripayattu is believed to have influenced other Asian martial arts and is often linked in folklore to the legendary sage Parashurama.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalaripayattu training traditionally includes stages such as Maithari (body control), Kolthari (wooden weapons), Ankathari (metal weapons), and Verumkai (bare-hand combat).

 

• Other indigenous Indian martial arts include Gatka (Punjab), Thang-Ta (Manipur), and Silambam (Tamil Nadu).

 

NOTE

 

• Gatka (Option 1): A traditional armed martial art associated with the Sikh community of Punjab, using sticks and swords, not originating in peninsular India.

 

• Muay Thai (Option 2): A striking martial art that originated in Thailand, not in India.

 

• Karate (Option 4): A striking martial art that originated in the Ryukyu Kingdom (present-day Okinawa, Japan), not in India.

question: In October 2022, which among the following substances was mapped in abundance for the first time, by Chandrayaan-2, on moon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In October 2022, the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter's CLASS (Chandrayaan-2 Large Area Soft X-ray Spectrometer) instrument mapped the abundance of sodium on the lunar surface for the first time. (चंद्रयान-2 — चंद्रमा पर सोडियम की प्रचुरता का पहली बार मानचित्रण)

 

• This achievement provided new insights into the thin lunar exosphere and how sodium atoms are distributed and released from the Moon's surface.

 

• The finding was significant because it opens possibilities for future studies on the sources and behaviour of sodium on the Moon's surface, which is relevant to understanding lunar weathering processes.

 

• ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) announced this achievement, adding to Chandrayaan-2's scientific contributions despite its lander mission not achieving a soft landing in 2019.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandrayaan-2 was launched in July 2019; while its lander Vikram crashed during landing, its orbiter has continued to function and deliver valuable scientific data.

 

• Chandrayaan-3, launched in 2023, successfully achieved a soft landing near the Moon's south pole in August 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrogen (Option 1): While hydrogen (as part of water-ice) has also been studied on the Moon by other missions, it was not the substance mapped in abundance for the first time by Chandrayaan-2 in October 2022.

 

• Chlorine (Option 2): Chlorine is not the substance associated with this particular Chandrayaan-2 CLASS finding from October 2022.

 

• Oxygen (Option 3): Oxygen (bound in lunar minerals) is well known to be present in lunar soil, but it is not the substance that was newly mapped in abundance for the first time by Chandrayaan-2 in October 2022.

question: Davis Cup is related with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Davis Cup is the world's premier international team competition in men's tennis, organized by the International Tennis Federation (ITF). (डेविस कप — पुरुष टेनिस की अंतरराष्ट्रीय टीम प्रतियोगिता)

 

• It was first held in 1900, originally as a challenge between the United States and Great Britain, and has since grown to include teams from across the world.

 

• Matches are contested between national teams in a knockout format, and it is often referred to as the "World Cup of Tennis."

 

• The trophy is named after Dwight F. Davis, an American tennis player who donated the original trophy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The women's equivalent of the Davis Cup is the Billie Jean King Cup (formerly known as the Fed Cup).

 

• India has a strong Davis Cup history, having reached the final three times (1966, 1974, and 1987), though it has never won the title.

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 1): International table tennis team competitions include the Swaythling Cup (men) and Corbillon Cup (women), not the Davis Cup.

 

• Cricket (Option 2): International cricket team trophies include the ICC Cricket World Cup and the Ashes; the Davis Cup is unrelated to cricket.

 

• Basketball (Option 3): International basketball competitions include the FIBA Basketball World Cup; the Davis Cup is not associated with basketball.

question: Who wrote the famous novel "Durgeshnandini"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Durgeshnandini" (1865) was the first novel written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, and it is widely regarded as one of the first modern novels in Bengali literature. (दुर्गेशनंदिनी — बंकिम चंद्र चट्टोपाध्याय की प्रथम रचना)

 

• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee is also the author of the famous novel "Anandamath" (1882), which contains the song "Vande Mataram", later adopted as India's national song.

 

• He served as a Deputy Magistrate in British India and made significant contributions to Bengali fiction, essays, and journalism, including founding the literary magazine "Bangadarshan."

 

• His works often blended historical fiction with themes of nationalism and social reform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• "Vande Mataram," penned by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, became a rallying cry during India's freedom struggle and was adopted as the National Song of India.

 

• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee is often referred to as one of the pioneers of the Indian novel in regional languages.

 

NOTE

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 1): A Nobel laureate (1913) known for works like "Gitanjali," "Gora," and the national anthem "Jana Gana Mana"; he did not write "Durgeshnandini."

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (Option 2): A noted social reformer and educator known for his contributions to women's education and widow remarriage, not for writing "Durgeshnandini."

 

• Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay (Option 4): A celebrated Bengali novelist known for works such as "Devdas" and "Parineeta," but he did not write "Durgeshnandini."

question: Which among the following is correct about Reverse Repo Rate?
option_1: Reverse Repo Rate is a state in which the Value of Money is Falling and the Prices are rising, over a period of time.
option_2: When bank deposit it’s excess money in RBI then RBI provides some interest to that bank. This interest is known as Reverse Repo Rate.
option_3: When RBI provides a loan to the bank for short-term between 1 to 90 days, RBI takes some interest from the bank which is termed as Reverse Repo Rate.
option_4: When the money is borrowed or lent for more than a day up to 14 days it is called Reverse Repo Rate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is "When bank deposit it's excess money in RBI then RBI provides some interest to that bank. This interest is known as Reverse Repo Rate."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reverse Repo Rate is the interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) borrows money from commercial banks by accepting their excess/surplus funds as deposits. (रिवर्स रेपो दर — RBI द्वारा बैंकों से अतिरिक्त राशि पर दिया जाने वाला ब्याज)

 

• When commercial banks have surplus liquidity, they park it with the RBI overnight (or for a short term), and in return, the RBI pays interest to the banks at the Reverse Repo Rate.

 

• It is essentially the opposite of the Repo Rate, where the RBI lends money to commercial banks against government securities, and the banks pay interest to RBI.

 

• The Reverse Repo Rate is a key tool used by the RBI to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system, helping control inflation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Reverse Repo Rate is normally kept lower than the Repo Rate, and the difference between them is called the "policy corridor."

 

• Both the Repo Rate and Reverse Repo Rate are important tools of RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), used to manage money supply and control inflation in the economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 describes inflation (a state where the value of money falls and prices rise over time), not the Reverse Repo Rate.

 

• Option 3 describes the Repo Rate, where the RBI lends money to banks for a short term and charges interest, not the Reverse Repo Rate.

 

• Option 4 describes features closer to short-term money market instruments/borrowing tenures in general, but this does not correctly define the Reverse Repo Rate mechanism.

question: The plains from Ambala to the Sunderban stretch over nearly 1800 km, but the fall in its slope is hardly ______ metres.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 300.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per NCERT geography, the Northern Plains of India stretch from Ambala in the west to the Sunderban delta in the east over a distance of nearly 1,800 km, but the total fall in elevation (slope) is hardly 300 metres. (उत्तरी मैदान — अंबाला से सुंदरबन तक की ढाल)

 

• This gives the Northern Plains an extremely gentle average slope, roughly around 15–20 cm per kilometre, making them one of the flattest and most fertile stretches of land in the world.

 

• These plains have been formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra river systems and their tributaries over thousands of years.

 

• The gentle gradient supports extensive irrigation, canal networks, and agriculture, making the Northern Plains the most densely populated and agriculturally productive region of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Northern Plains are typically divided into four regions: the Bhabar, the Tarai, the Bhangar, and the Khadar.

 

• Despite their vast length, the plains vary in width from about 90 km to 300 km, being narrower in the east (Assam) and wider in the Punjab-Haryana region.

 

NOTE

 

• 550 (Option 1): This figure does not match the NCERT-cited total fall in slope for the plains from Ambala to Sunderban.

 

• 600 (Option 3): This value is incorrect for this specific geographic fact.

 

• 450 (Option 4): This value is also incorrect for the total fall in slope described in this NCERT reference.

question: In which of the following modes of data transmission, can the data flow in both directions but in only one direction at a time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Half-duplex.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Half-duplex mode, data can be transmitted in both directions, but only one direction at a time — i.e., a device can either send or receive at a given moment, not both simultaneously. (हाफ-डुप्लेक्स — दोनों दिशाओं में परंतु एक समय में एक दिशा में डेटा प्रवाह)

 

• A common real-world example of half-duplex communication is a walkie-talkie, where only one party can speak at a time while the other listens.

 

• Half-duplex is more efficient than simplex (which allows only one-way communication) but less efficient than full-duplex (which allows simultaneous two-way communication).

 

• This concept is a fundamental part of data communication and computer networking, describing how devices exchange information over a communication channel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A common example of a full-duplex system is a telephone conversation, where both parties can speak and listen at the same time.

 

• A common example of a simplex system is a traditional television broadcast, where signals flow only from the broadcaster to the receiver, never the reverse.

 

NOTE

 

• Simplex (Option 2): In simplex mode, data flows in only one direction, never the reverse — for example, from a keyboard to a computer.

 

• Full-duplex (Option 3): In full-duplex mode, data can flow in both directions simultaneously — for example, in a telephone call.

 

• Quarter-duplex (Option 4): This is not a standard/recognized term in data transmission terminology.

question: Which among the following is the highest peak in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanchenjunga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kanchenjunga, standing at 8,586 metres, is generally considered the highest peak located within India, situated on the border between Sikkim (India) and Nepal. (कंचनजंगा — भारत की सबसे ऊँची चोटी)

 

• It is also the third-highest mountain in the world, after Mount Everest and K2.

 

• Kanchenjunga is part of the Himalayan mountain range and is considered sacred by the local Sikkimese people, who traditionally do not climb to its exact summit out of respect for local beliefs.

 

• Although K2 (8,611 m) is taller, it lies in the Pakistan-administered region of Kashmir, so for the purposes of Indian geography, Kanchenjunga is cited as the highest peak within Indian territory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The name "Kanchenjunga" is derived from Tibetan words meaning "The Five Treasures of the Great Snow," referring to its five peaks representing gold, silver, gems, grain, and holy books.

 

• Kanchenjunga National Park in Sikkim is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its unique biodiversity and cultural significance.

 

NOTE

 

• Nanga Parbat (Option 2): The ninth-highest mountain in the world (8,126 m), located in the Pakistan-administered region of Kashmir, not in Indian-administered territory.

 

• Nanda Devi (Option 3): The second-highest peak located entirely within India (7,816 m), situated in Uttarakhand, but lower than Kanchenjunga.

 

• Namcha Barwa (Option 4): A peak located in Tibet, China, near the great bend of the Yarlung Tsangpo (Brahmaputra) river, not in India.

question: In October 2022, according to UN Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), which country has the largest number of poor people worldwide?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report, released in October 2022 by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI), found that India had the largest number of people living in multidimensional poverty worldwide, at nearly 228.9 million people. (वैश्विक बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2022 — भारत सबसे अधिक गरीब जनसंख्या)

 

• Despite this, the report also highlighted that India made significant progress, with about 415 million people moving out of multidimensional poverty between 2005–06 and 2019–21.

 

• The Multidimensional Poverty Index measures poverty across three dimensions — health, education, and standard of living — using multiple indicators rather than income alone.

 

• The report was based on data largely drawn from India's National Family Health Survey (NFHS).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The MPI framework was developed jointly by OPHI and UNDP and has been published annually as part of the UNDP's Human Development Report initiative since 2010.

 

• Along with India, countries like Nigeria, Pakistan, Ethiopia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo also featured among the nations with large numbers of multidimensionally poor populations.

 

NOTE

 

• Nigeria (Option 1): Nigeria had a large multidimensionally poor population and featured prominently in the report, but it did not have the largest number worldwide.

 

• Indonesia (Option 2): Indonesia was not among the countries with the largest number of poor people according to the 2022 Global MPI report.

 

• Pakistan (Option 3): Pakistan also had a significant multidimensionally poor population, but it was not the country with the highest number worldwide.

question: Neelima performs Kalbeliya dance form. Which state does this dance form belong to?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalbeliya is a traditional folk dance performed by the Kalbeliya community (traditionally associated with snake charming) of Rajasthan. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — राजस्थान की लोक नृत्य शैली)

 

• It is performed by women in flowing black skirts, embroidered with silver ribbons, mimicking the movements of a serpent along with quick swirling movements and acrobatic postures.

 

• Kalbeliya songs and dances were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

• The dance is traditionally accompanied by instruments like the been (pungi), dholak, and khanjari.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Chari, and Bhavai.

 

• Rajasthan is renowned for its rich folk music and dance traditions, closely tied to the state's various communities and their historical occupations.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Punjab is known for folk dances such as Bhangra and Giddha, not Kalbeliya.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Uttarakhand is known for folk dances such as Chholiya and Langvir Nritya, not Kalbeliya.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): Odisha is known for classical and folk dances such as Odissi and Gotipua, not Kalbeliya.

question: Which of the following music instruments are solid instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghana Vadya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the traditional Indian classification of musical instruments, Ghana Vadya refers to solid (idiophonic) instruments that produce sound by the striking of one solid part against another, without the use of strings, membranes, or air columns. (घन वाद्य — ठोस वाद्य यंत्र)

 

• Examples of Ghana Vadya include the Manjira (cymbals), Jaltarang, Ghatam, and Kartal.

 

• Indian musical instruments are traditionally classified into four broad categories: Tata (string), Sushira (wind), Avanaddha (percussion with membrane), and Ghana (solid/idiophonic).

 

• Ghana Vadyas are among the oldest categories of instruments and are often used to maintain rhythm in devotional and folk music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ghatam, a clay pot instrument, is a well-known Ghana Vadya widely used in Carnatic classical music.

 

• This four-fold classification of Indian musical instruments closely parallels the international Hornbostel-Sachs system, which divides instruments into idiophones, membranophones, chordophones, and aerophones.

 

NOTE

 

• Tata Vadya (Option 1): These are stringed instruments, such as the sitar, veena, and sarod, where sound is produced by the vibration of strings.

 

• Avanaddha Vadya (Option 3): These are membranophones/percussion instruments covered with a membrane, such as the tabla, mridangam, and dholak.

 

• Sushira Vadya (Option 4): These are wind instruments, such as the flute (bansuri) and shehnai, where sound is produced by blowing air through them.

question: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) is the ambitious program launched by Government of India in 2018 to provide ______ access to the most vulnerable sections.
solution_text:
The correct answer is healthcare.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) is an ambitious health insurance scheme launched by the Government of India in 2018 to provide healthcare access to the most vulnerable and economically weaker sections of society. (प्रधानमंत्री जन आरोग्य योजना — गरीब वर्गों को स्वास्थ्य सुविधा)

 

• It provides a health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization, on a cashless and paperless basis.

 

• PM-JAY is a key component of Ayushman Bharat, India's flagship health protection scheme, and is considered one of the largest government-funded healthcare programs in the world.

 

• The scheme is implemented by the National Health Authority (NHA) and benefits around 50 crore (500 million) individuals belonging to poor and vulnerable families, based on deprivation and occupational criteria from the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM-JAY was launched on 23 September 2018 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and is often referred to as "Modicare."

 

• The scheme covers pre-existing diseases from day one and includes a wide range of medical and surgical procedures across empanelled public and private hospitals.

 

NOTE

 

• services (Option 2): This term is too generic and does not correctly complete the description of PM-JAY's specific purpose, which is healthcare access.

 

• agricultural (Option 3): PM-JAY is unrelated to agriculture; agricultural welfare schemes include PM-KISAN and the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana.

 

• industrial (Option 4): PM-JAY is unrelated to industrial development; it is specifically a healthcare access and insurance scheme.

question: A ball possesses 3000 units of momentum. What would be the ball’s new momentum if its velocity was doubled?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6000 units.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Momentum (p) of an object is given by the formula p = m × v, where m is the mass and v is the velocity of the object. (संवेग = द्रव्यमान × वेग)

 

• Momentum is directly proportional to velocity when the mass of the object remains constant.

 

• Since the ball's mass does not change, doubling the velocity will result in the momentum also being doubled.

 

• Given the initial momentum is 3000 units, doubling the velocity gives a new momentum of 3000 × 2 = 6000 units.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Momentum is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction, and its SI unit is kg·m/s.

 

• The concept of momentum conservation is fundamental to understanding collisions in physics — in the absence of external forces, the total momentum of a system remains constant.

 

NOTE

 

• 3000 units (Option 1): This would only be correct if the velocity remained unchanged, which contradicts the condition given in the question.

 

• 20000 units (Option 3): This value does not correspond to simply doubling the velocity; it is not mathematically consistent with p = mv.

 

• 9000 units (Option 4): This would correspond to tripling the momentum, not doubling the velocity as stated in the question.

question: Who among the following appointed Aziz Khummar a wine distiller to high administrative post?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Tughluq.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the medieval chronicler Ziauddin Barani, Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq appointed people from humble or "low" professional backgrounds to high administrative posts, a practice that was heavily criticized by contemporary court historians. (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक — निम्न वर्ग के व्यक्तियों की उच्च पदों पर नियुक्ति)

 

• Among those appointed was Aziz Khummar, a wine distiller, along with others such as Firuz Hajjam (a barber) and Manka Tabbakh (a cook), who were elevated to important administrative positions.

 

• Barani, in his work "Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi," viewed this as a violation of the traditional social hierarchy and criticized Muhammad bin Tughluq for disregarding birth and lineage in making these appointments.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughluq is well known in history for several bold and controversial administrative experiments, including the transfer of capital to Daulatabad and the introduction of token currency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muhammad bin Tughluq ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1325 to 1351 CE and is often described by historians as a ruler of brilliant ideas but flawed implementation.

 

• Ziauddin Barani was a court historian during the reigns of Muhammad bin Tughluq and Firuz Shah Tughluq, and his chronicles remain a key source for understanding the socio-political conditions of the era.

 

NOTE

 

• Alauddin Khalji (Option 1): Known for his market control reforms and military campaigns, particularly against the Mongols and in the Deccan; he is not associated with this specific appointment.

 

• Jalaluddin Khalji (Option 3): The founder of the Khalji dynasty, known for his relatively lenient rule; he is not associated with this specific appointment.

 

• Firuz Shah Tughluq (Option 4): Successor of Muhammad bin Tughluq, known for public welfare works and the introduction of Islamic taxes like Jizya in a stricter form; he is not associated with this specific appointment.

question: Which among the following is a bacterial disease?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leprosy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Leprosy, also known as Hansen's Disease, is caused by the bacterium *Mycobacterium leprae*, making it a bacterial disease. (कुष्ठ रोग — जीवाणु जनित रोग)

 

• It primarily affects the skin, peripheral nerves, mucous membranes, and eyes, and if left untreated, can lead to progressive and permanent disabilities.

 

• Leprosy is curable with Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT), which is provided free of cost under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) in India.

 

• India has historically had one of the highest burdens of leprosy cases in the world, though the disease has been significantly controlled through sustained public health efforts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• World Leprosy Day is observed annually on the last Sunday of January to raise awareness and reduce stigma associated with the disease.

 

• India officially achieved the WHO-defined elimination target for leprosy (less than 1 case per 10,000 population) at the national level in 2005, though pockets of higher prevalence remain in some areas.

 

NOTE

 

• Rabies (Option 1): A viral disease caused by the rabies virus (Lyssavirus), transmitted mainly through the bite of infected animals, particularly dogs.

 

• Malaria (Option 3): A disease caused by a protozoan parasite of the genus *Plasmodium*, transmitted through the bite of an infected female *Anopheles* mosquito — not a bacterial disease.

 

• Ebola (Option 4): A severe viral hemorrhagic fever caused by the Ebola virus, primarily spread through contact with bodily fluids of infected individuals or animals.
